gaps: Portfolio titles are LLBC portfolio names with 'Minister of' prepended. The original LLBC wording is in llbc_portfolio wherever the rendering differs. The combined Provincial Secretary titles, such as 'Provincial Secretary and Minister of Government Services', are my rendering of LLBC's 'Provincial Secretary and Government Services'. I did not confirm the exact commission wording.

LLBC ends every W.R. Bennett appointment on 6 Aug 1986, and Vander Zalm holdovers begin that day, even though most ministers served on without reappointment. Vander Zalm-era holdovers likewise end on 2 Apr 1991 and resume in the Johnston records.

Premier appointments are omitted, as instructed. The Premier's President of the Council appointments are included for Bennett, Vander Zalm and Johnston, along with Bennett's Energy, Transport and Communications (1978) and Vander Zalm's Finance (1986).

Deputy Premier is included even though it headed no department. Periods with no Deputy Premier (1983-05-26 to 1986-08-14 and 1986-11-06 to 1990-08-10) have no records. Ministers of state (1987-1989 regional ministers) are excluded.

Vacancies with no holder: Transport portfolios during parts of 1976-78 were merged into Energy, Transport and Communications. Forests and Municipal Affairs were vacant 1986-08-11 to 1986-08-14. Economic Development was vacant from 1988-07-05 until it was disestablished on 1988-07-06. Attorney General was officially vacant 1988-06-29 to 1988-07-06 (Veitch acted informally). Advanced Education and Job Training was officially vacant 1987-07-29 to 1987-08-06 (Brian Smith acted informally). Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources was vacant 1991-03-28 to 1991-04-15.

Acting ministers named routinely by OIC for a minister's absence are not covered by LLBC and are not recorded. The acting records here are informal actings reported in the press, or cases where powers were transferred by OIC without designating a minister.

Wikipedia's Vander Zalm table disagrees with LLBC in several places. It gives Veitch as acting AG to 1988-08-06 and Bud Smith from 1988-08-06; LLBC has Bud Smith from 1988-07-06. It collapses renamed portfolios such as Municipal Affairs and Transit, Continuing Education and Job Training, and Tourism, Recreation and Culture. It lists Labour and Consumer Services under Segarty from 1986; LLBC has 'Labour' until 1986-11-06. LLBC was preferred throughout.
Norm Jacobsen stepped out of Social Services and Housing from about 28 Jun to 19 Jul 1991 for the leadership race. No OIC was issued and no replacement is known.

Holder names use common forms (e.g. 'Tony Brummet' for Anthony Julius Brummet, 'Bud Smith' for Stuart Douglas Boland Smith, 'Russ Fraser' for Russell Gordon Fraser, 'Norm Jacobsen' for Johan Alvin Norman Jacobsen); LLBC gives full legal names.
